findings.title: Batch tenant lookup always receives an empty ID list
findings.failure: Records with nonempty tenantExternalIds are excluded from recordsWithTenantStubs, so this lookup receives no IDs. Nango customer imports omit existing tenant memberships; tenant-centric jobs skip those customers entirely. Rolling back the code does not restore records already skipped by a one-off import.
findings.fix: Collect external IDs from inRecords, or from records filtered for nonempty tenantExternalIds. Verify both the lookup count and resulting memberships.
findings.evidence: Lines 484–487 select only records whose tenantExternalIds are absent or empty; lines 510–512 read IDs from that selection. HEAD~1 looked up each record’s IDs directly. The existing membership assertion at importCustomers.tenants.litest.ts:152 and the new lookup assertion at :202 both contradict the new path.

findings.title: Single-customer imports no longer look up existing tenants
findings.failure: When tenantsByExternalId is omitted, importCustomer substitutes an empty map and silently omits tenant memberships. Thread, message-author, and embedded-customer imports call importCustomer without that map.
findings.fix: When no map is supplied, retain the previous aggregate lookup and return its error through scope.fail.
findings.evidence: Direct callers in importThreads.ts:140, importThreadMessage.ts:150, and importAllCustomersAndUsersInRecords.ts:59 pass only record. HEAD~1 importCustomers.ts:301–307 queried getTenantsFromIdentifiers for these records.

findings.title: A failed tenant lookup becomes a successful partial import
findings.failure: Once the batch receives actual IDs, a permission or database lookup error is logged and skipped. The import then treats those tenants as missing, omitting memberships or skipping tenant-centric customers while reporting success.
findings.fix: Return Result.err(lookupResult.error) from the helper and let importCustomers return the failure.
findings.evidence: The new helper uses continue on isErr and unconditionally returns Result.ok at line 290. HEAD~1 importCustomer returned scope.fail on the same lookup error at lines 304–305.

findings.title: The no-op fast path drops import-job attribution updates
findings.failure: An otherwise unchanged customer imported under a new job returns NOOP before importedByJobDefinitionId is updated. The stored customer remains attributed to the old job or null.
findings.fix: Pass importedByJobDefinitionId to shouldPerformCustomerUpsertUpdate in the fast path, and cover an unchanged customer whose job definition changes.
findings.evidence: The transactional path passes the field at customerAggregate.ts:1025–1033 and writes it at :1060–1062. shouldPerformCustomerUpsertUpdate.ts:16–21 explicitly treats a changed job ID as an update; its tests at :105–111 cover that case. Nango passes the job ID at handleImportSyncMessage.ts:173–175.

findings.title: The new batch error branch is unreachable
findings.failure: The isErr branch cannot execute because getTenantsByExternalId returns Result.ok on every completed path, including failed lookups.
findings.fix: Propagate lookup errors from the helper so this branch handles them.
findings.evidence: The helper’s only return is Result.ok at line 290. A tracked-code search, `git grep -n 'getTenantsByExternalId' HEAD -- packages services lambdas infra terraform migrations testing test`, found only its definition and this call.

findings.title: Use a structured field in the new error log
findings.failure: The new log interpolates identifier.type with %s, departing from this repository’s required structured logging pattern.
findings.fix: Log `{ err: existingCustomerResult.error, identifierType: identifier.type }` with a fixed message.
findings.evidence: The supplied AGENTS.md Logging section requires structured logs and says never to use %s interpolation. The new call passes identifier.type as a format argument at lines 651–655.

Data and rollback: no delete, retention, or schema one-way door was added; missed imports and attribution need replay or repair after a rollback.
Operability and blast radius: no redeploy trigger or shared constant changed; shared upsert callers were traced, with the job-attribution regression reported above.
Review used only local HEAD and HEAD~1 code. No network calls, file edits, or tests were run.
